_publication.note: Published copy for documentation. Sanitized on 2026-09-25 PT: local file paths, cache paths, account names and people's names were removed or generalized; the question text, closed sets, thresholds and fail-closed rules are unchanged. This contract embeds NO real posts, X post text, author handles, term example posts, holdout ids or database contents: the {term}/{pid}/STATE fields are template placeholders filled at run time. The illustrative state under 'synthetic_example' (where present) is invented and clearly synthetic.

provenance: NEW 2026-09-25 11:07 PT, rebuilt-series label (not an original contract). Synonym-split fix (meaning field only, not verdicts). Changes vs v1: (1) near-duplicate candidates are merged before scoring (Jev pairwise same-sense check, complete linkage) so synonyms no longer split probability; (2) corpus/evidence notes are no longer candidates; (3) when no stored gloss resolves, a second stage offers short meanings taken verbatim from the term's own slang-sense posts (deterministic 'X means / stands for / = ...' extraction). Jev only returns choice/boolean/score answers, so it cannot write free text and nothing is invented. Same confidence + post-agreement bar as v1.

merge.representative: first member in candidate order (stored glosses before post-derived)

note: A context meaning (INFERRED) fills the note's meaning field only; it is NOT attestation and never changes a verdict. An operator definition (OBSERVED) overrides it. Context first; the operator is asked only when context cannot settle the meaning (UNRESOLVED).

merge.instructions: STATE.candidates are short candidate meanings for the slang term '{term}'. Do candidates {a} and {b} describe the same sense of the term (paraphrases or near-synonyms of one meaning), rather than different meanings?

overall.instructions: STATE.posts are posts that use the term '{term}' as slang. Each option lists one meaning (alternative phrasings of the same meaning are separated by ' | '). Which option best describes how the term is used in these posts? Pick an option only if most posts fit it. Pick NONE_FIT if no option fits the posts, MIXED if the posts use clearly different senses with none dominant.

criteria_extra.NONE_FIT: no listed meaning fits how the posts use the term
criteria_extra.MIXED: posts use clearly different senses; none dominant

support.instructions: Post {pid} in STATE.posts: is the term '{term}' used there in the sense given in STATE.meaning (same or a close variant of that sense)? Mentioning or explaining the term with that sense counts as SUPPORTS.

criteria.SUPPORTS: uses or explains the term in STATE.meaning's sense (or a close variant)
criteria.DIFFERENT: uses the term in a different sense, or the post does not show the sense
